title: French v English
summary: A high-energy team dodgeball game with a rope divide, foam balls and a rescue mission.
setup: Lay the rope across the middle of the hall.
Put one chair at the back of each team’s area.
Split the section into two even teams and share out the foam balls.
steps: Teams start in their own half. Nobody may cross the rope.
Players throw foam balls at the other team. A ball only counts if it hits below the shoulders.
If a player is hit, they cross to the other team’s back area and stand on the chair.
To free a teammate, a player still in the game must throw them a ball and they must catch it without stepping off the chair.
A caught ball frees the player, who returns to their own half. If the catch is dropped, they stay on the chair.
Play until one team has no players left in their half, or until time is called.
winning: The team with the most players still in their own half when time is called wins. You can also play until one team is completely captured.
safety: Use soft foam balls only and aim below the shoulders. Keep the area around the chairs clear, and make sure players step down carefully. Balls that roll across the rope can be collected by the team on that side.

tips.title: Keep the game moving
tips.text: Have a leader return stray balls so nobody is left waiting for a turn.

tips.title: Make the rescue clear
tips.text: Mark a small jail area around each chair so players know exactly where to stand.

tips.title: Team talk
tips.text: Pause halfway for a 30-second huddle so teams can plan who will rescue who.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Let players sit on a bench instead of standing on a chair, and use a larger, softer ball.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Players must throw with their non-dominant hand, or only one-handed catches count.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Give every player a rescue partner and allow a walking-only version. Players who prefer not to throw can be official ball collectors or chair spotters.

themedTwists.title: Pumpkin Dodge
themedTwists.text: Use orange balls and play spooky music. Players do a silly pumpkin pose when they are caught.

themedTwists.title: Meteor Rescue
themedTwists.text: Call the balls meteors and the chairs moon bases. Players float back to their half with slow-motion moon steps.

author: Games library team

title: Crab Football
summary: Football with a twist: everyone plays on their hands and feet with their chest facing the sky.
setup: Mark a pitch with cones and a goal at each end.
Split into two teams and give out bibs.
Show everyone the crab position: hands and feet on the floor, tummy facing up.
steps: Everyone starts in the crab position. Players move on their hands and feet, keeping their chest facing the sky.
Pass and shoot using feet only. No standing up and no using hands on the ball.
A goal is scored when the ball crosses between the cones.
After a goal, both teams return to their own half and restart from the centre.
Rotate goalkeepers every few minutes so everyone gets a turn in a different role.
winning: The team with the most goals at the end of the match wins. For a shorter game, play first to three goals.
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders first. Check the floor for slippery patches and use a soft ball indoors. No sliding tackles, and keep the pitch clear of bags and chairs.

tips.title: Short bursts
tips.text: Play in three-minute bursts with a quick rest between them. Crab football is hard work on the arms.

tips.title: Referee together
tips.text: Use two young leaders as referees so more of the section stays involved.

tips.title: Celebrate the falls
tips.text: A silly crab dance after every goal keeps the mood light and stops players worrying about falling over.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Play seated crab football, or use a larger goal and a lighter ball.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Players must keep one hand off the floor at all times, or goals only count if scored from their own half.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Have rolling substitutions and let players choose to be a crab goalkeeper, referee or commentator.

themedTwists.title: Spider Football
themedTwists.text: The rules stay exactly the same. Teams are spiders, the goals are webs and every pass is a web-sling.

themedTwists.title: Reindeer Football
themedTwists.text: Same crab football rules, but players wear antlers and the ball has a red nose.

themedTwists.title: Moon Crab Football
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with slow-motion moon moves and a countdown before every restart.

author: Games library team

title: Dodgeball
summary: The classic team game: dodge, catch and throw your way to the last player standing.
setup: Mark a centre line and a back line for each team.
Place the balls along the centre line.
Split into two teams and stand them behind their back lines.
steps: On the count of three, teams run to collect the balls from the centre line.
Players throw from behind their own back line. Balls must hit below the shoulders to count.
A player who is hit sits out at the side. A player who catches a ball on the full earns a life and can bring one teammate back in.
Balls that stop in a team’s half belong to that team. Do not cross the centre line to collect them.
Play until one team has no players left, or until time is called.
winning: The last team with players still in the game wins. If time runs out, the team with more players left wins.
safety: Use soft foam balls only. No headshots, no throwing at players who are sitting out, and no running with a ball above shoulder height. Keep the side lines clear.

tips.title: Equal teams
tips.text: Mix ages and abilities across both teams rather than letting friendship groups choose.

tips.title: Quick restarts
tips.text: Keep spare balls at the side so the game does not stop every time a ball rolls away.

tips.title: Change the rules
tips.text: Try a ‘no running’ round or a ‘non-dominant hand’ round to keep things fresh.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a larger, slower ball and allow players to deflect with their hands.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Shrink the court, add a ‘no blocking’ rule, or make catches worth two lives.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use rolling balls instead of throws, or give every player a ‘shield’ card that blocks one hit.

themedTwists.title: Meteor Dodgeball
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the balls are meteors and players must freeze like astronauts when a meteor passes.

themedTwists.title: Ghost Dodgeball
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with spooky music and a ghostly ‘boo’ every time a player is out.

author: Games library team

title: Capture the Flag
summary: A wide game of sneaking, sprinting and jailbreaks that gets the whole section moving.
setup: Set clear boundaries and walk them with everyone before the game.
Mark a base and a jail for each team, with the flag visible in the base.
Split into two teams and place one adult marshal at each jail.
steps: Each team defends its own flag while trying to steal the other team’s flag.
A player can only be tagged while they are in the other team’s half.
Tagged players go to the opposition jail. They can be freed when a teammate tags them.
If a player is tagged while carrying the flag, they must drop it and it returns to its base.
The first team to carry the opposition flag back to its own base wins.
If nobody has won after the time limit, the team that got closest to the flag wins.
winning: Capture the other team’s flag and bring it back to your base, or be the team closest to a capture when time is called.
safety: Walk the boundaries together and keep them away from roads, water and steep ground. No tackling or grabbing. Keep a headcount at the start, middle and end, and have an adult marshal at each jail.

tips.title: Use clear flags
tips.text: Bright cloths tied to a pole are easier to see than a flag lying on the ground.

tips.title: Rotate roles
tips.text: Ask each team to choose two defenders and two attackers for the first five minutes, then swap.

tips.title: Make the jail obvious
tips.text: Mark the jail with cones and a marshal so freed players know where to go.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a smaller area, shorten the jail time to 30 seconds, or let freed players rejoin without a tag.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add two flags per team, or make players walk instead of run while carrying the flag.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Create a ‘safe zone’ near each base. Players who prefer not to run can be flag guards, jail marshals or code-makers.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Treasure
themedTwists.text: The flags become treasure chests. Same rules, with pirate names for the bases and jail.

themedTwists.title: Jungle Flag
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but players must move like a jungle animal of their choice between bases.

author: Games library team

title: Bench Ball
summary: A team passing game where the goal is to get the ball into the hands of your player on the bench.
setup: Put one bench at each end of the hall.
Mark a no-go zone around each bench.
Split into two teams and choose one player to stand on each bench.
steps: Teams pass the ball to each other and try to get it to their player on the bench.
Players cannot run with the ball. They can take two steps before passing or shooting.
A point is scored when the bench player catches the ball without stepping off the bench.
After a point, the bench player swaps with a teammate and the game restarts from the centre.
Defenders must stay at least one metre away from the bench player.
winning: The team with the most catches by bench players at the end of the game wins.
safety: Use a soft ball and keep the benches stable. No jumping onto or off the bench, and no pushing near the no-go zone. Check that the bench can take the weight of a player.

tips.title: Spread out
tips.text: Encourage teams to use the whole width of the hall rather than crowding around the bench.

tips.title: Rotate often
tips.text: Swap bench players every two points so everyone gets a turn.

tips.title: Count together
tips.text: Ask a young leader to keep the score on a whiteboard so everyone can see it.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow bench players to step down and catch, or use a larger ball.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Bench players must catch with one hand, or the ball must be passed three times before a shot.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use a rolling ball instead of a thrown ball, and let players choose to be a bench player, defender or referee.

themedTwists.title: Space Station Catch
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the benches are space stations and every pass is a ‘docking manoeuvre’.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Sleigh
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a sleigh bell on the bench and Christmas music between points.

author: Games library team

title: Stuck in the Mud
summary: A simple, brilliant tag game that works with any size of group and needs almost no equipment.
setup: Mark a clear playing area with cones.
Choose two or three taggers and give them bibs.
Walk through the freeze and rescue rules before you start.
steps: Taggers count to five while everyone else spreads out.
If a tagger touches you, you freeze on the spot with your feet apart.
A free player can rescue you by high-fiving your hand or ducking under your arm.
Once rescued, you are back in the game and can rescue others.
Change taggers every few minutes so everyone gets a turn.
winning: There is no winner: the aim is to keep everyone moving. If you want a challenge, the last player to be frozen becomes the next tagger.
safety: Walk or jog rather than sprint. Tag below the shoulders and keep the area clear. If players duck under arms, show them how to do it gently and only on a soft surface.

tips.title: Freeze poses
tips.text: Let players choose a silly frozen pose. It makes the game funnier and easier to spot who is out.

tips.title: Smaller area
tips.text: For Beavers, shrink the area so rescues happen quickly and nobody is stuck for long.

tips.title: Team rescue
tips.text: Try a rule where two players must high-five a frozen player together.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use walking taggers, or give every player three ‘lives’ before they have to freeze.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a second set of taggers after two minutes, or make rescued players do five star jumps before rejoining.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a ‘rescue station’ where players can free themselves once, and let players who prefer not to run be taggers or cone marshals.

themedTwists.title: Frozen in the Mud
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but frozen players strike a snowman pose and rescuers give them a warm-up high-five.

themedTwists.title: Jungle Mud
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with animal noises for each rescue and a ‘swamp’ area marked with cones.

themedTwists.title: Zombie Mud
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but frozen players groan like zombies until they are rescued.

author: Games library team

title: Sharks and Minnows
summary: A running and dodging game where the minnows try to cross the pool without being caught.
setup: Mark two safe lines at opposite ends of the hall.
Choose one or two sharks to stand in the middle.
Line the minnows up behind one safe line.
steps: The sharks call ‘minnows, swim!’ and the minnows try to run to the other safe line.
If a shark tags a minnow, that minnow becomes seaweed and stands still in the middle.
Seaweed can tag minnows as they run past, but must keep one foot on their spot.
The last minnow becomes the next shark.
Start again with a new round and new sharks.
winning: The last minnow left is the winner and gets to be the next shark.
safety: Use walking or fast walking for Beavers. Keep the running lanes clear and make sure seaweed players stand still with their arms out gently, not grabbing.

tips.title: More sharks
tips.text: Start with two sharks so the first round does not take too long.

tips.title: Clear lanes
tips.text: Put cones down the sides to mark the running area and stop players cutting corners.

tips.title: Seaweed freeze
tips.text: Seaweed must keep both feet still and tag with a gentle touch, not a grab.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter crossing distance and walking sharks.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘no stopping’ rule, or make the sharks choose a new move for each round.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players who prefer not to run be seaweed straight away, or give every minnow a ‘safe pass’ card.

themedTwists.title: Jellyfish Tag
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but seaweed players wobble their arms like jellyfish and everyone makes a sea sound when tagged.

themedTwists.title: Space Invaders
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with asteroids for seaweed and a countdown before each crossing.

author: Games library team

title: Grandma’s Footsteps
summary: A classic quiet-to-loud game of sneaking up on Grandma without being spotted.
setup: Choose one player to be Grandma and stand them at one end of the hall facing away from the group.
Line everyone else up at the other end.
Explain that players must freeze whenever Grandma turns around.
steps: Grandma stands with their back to the group and counts to five.
Everyone creeps forward while Grandma is facing away.
Grandma can turn around at any time. Anyone still moving must return to the start line.
The first player to reach Grandma and tap them gently on the shoulder becomes the next Grandma.
If nobody reaches Grandma after a few minutes, choose a new Grandma and start again.
winning: The first player to reach Grandma and tap their shoulder wins and takes the next turn.
safety: Walking only, no running. Keep the start line clear and make sure players do not bump into each other when they freeze.

tips.title: Silly turns
tips.text: Let Grandma strike a funny pose when they turn around to make the game harder to resist.

tips.title: Count slowly
tips.text: Grandma should count at different speeds so players cannot predict when they will turn.

tips.title: No elimination
tips.text: Sending players back to the start is enough. Nobody sits out.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Grandma counts to ten and only turns around after a loud clap.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Players must move in a silly walk, or Grandma can turn around twice in a row.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Allow players to take three big steps from the start line, and let anyone who prefers not to move be the caller.

themedTwists.title: Sleeping Pirates
themedTwists.text: Grandma becomes the sleeping pirate. Same rules, but players must creep like they are on a ship.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Footsteps
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with Santa’s hat on the caller and a jingle bell that rings when they turn.

author: Games library team

title: Captain’s Coming
summary: A fast reaction game where the leader calls out ship commands and everyone races to follow.
setup: Mark one side of the hall as the bow and the other as the stern.
Mark port and starboard with cones.
Practise each command once before starting.
steps: The leader calls out a command and everyone performs the action as quickly as possible.
Bow: run to the front. Stern: run to the back. Port: run to the left. Starboard: run to the right.
Other commands can include ‘scrub the deck’, ‘climb the rigging’, ‘man overboard’ and ‘captain’s coming’ (salute and stand still).
The last person to react does a silly forfeit, then rejoins the game.
Speed up the calls and add new commands as the group gets confident.
winning: There is no single winner: the aim is to keep everyone moving and laughing. For a competition, give points to the first three players to react correctly.
safety: Use walking or jogging only and keep the floor clear. Make sure port and starboard are obvious from every part of the hall. Demonstrate each move before calling it.

tips.title: Start slow
tips.text: Teach four commands first, then add two more once the group knows them.

tips.title: Silly forfeits
tips.text: Forfeits should be quick and kind: a salute, a pirate laugh or five star jumps.

tips.title: Young leaders
tips.text: Let a young leader be the captain for a round while an adult watches the edges.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use only four commands and point to the correct side while calling.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Call commands faster, add a ‘opposite’ rule, or remove the cones.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version with arm actions, and let players choose to be the caller or the judge.

themedTwists.title: Astronaut’s Orders
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with commands like ‘boosters’, ‘gravity off’ and ‘alien spotted’. Everyone floats between moves.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Coming
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with commands like ‘load the sleigh’, ‘check the list’ and ‘ho ho ho’.

author: Games library team

title: Zip Zap Boing
summary: A quick-fire name game that builds concentration and gets a lot of laughs.
setup: Stand everyone in a circle with enough space to move an arm.
Practise saying each other’s names before starting.
Explain the three moves: zip, zap and boing.
steps: ‘Zip’ passes to the person on your left or right. Say their name and make a zip gesture.
‘Zap’ passes across the circle to anyone. Point at them and say their name.
‘Boing’ bounces the move back to the person who sent it. Hold up both hands like a spring.
If someone hesitates, says the wrong name or makes the wrong gesture, they do a quick forfeit and the game carries on.
Add a second ball or a ‘reverse’ command once the group is confident.
winning: There is no winner: the aim is to keep the rally going. For a challenge, count how many passes the group can make without a mistake.
safety: No throwing or physical contact. Keep the circle wide enough that players can gesture without hitting each other.

tips.title: Names first
tips.text: Use name badges for the first few rounds so new members are not put on the spot.

tips.title: One rule at a time
tips.text: Play with zip and zap only, then add boing once the group has the hang of it.

tips.title: Fast forfeits
tips.text: A forfeit should take five seconds: a bow, a silly face or a victory dance.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow players to say their own name as they pass, or point instead of speaking.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add ‘reverse’, ‘double zip’ or a second ball.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use gestures and signs alongside names, and let players sit in the circle if standing is difficult.

themedTwists.title: Santa Zap
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but players pass a pretend present and say ‘ho ho ho’ instead of boing.

themedTwists.title: Alien Zap
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with alien noises and a ‘warp speed’ round where everything speeds up.

author: Games library team

title: Splat
summary: A high-speed circle game that helps everyone learn names and react quickly.
setup: Stand in a circle with one player in the middle.
Practise the names of the two players on either side of each person.
Explain that ‘splat’ is a silly word, not a physical action.
steps: The player in the middle points at someone and says ‘splat!’
That player ducks down. The two players on either side of them point at each other and say ‘splat’ as fast as they can.
The slower of the two goes into the middle. If the pointed-at player forgets to duck, they go into the middle instead.
Keep the game moving quickly and encourage everyone to say names as they play.
After a few rounds, swap the word for a themed sound or action.
winning: There is no winner: the aim is to keep the circle moving and learn names. For a competition, count how many rounds each player survives.
safety: No physical splatting. Ducking should be gentle and controlled, with enough space between players. Stop if anyone feels dizzy from ducking.

tips.title: Names, not just splat
tips.text: Ask players to say the other person’s name before splat to help everyone learn names.

tips.title: Smaller circles
tips.text: Use two circles for a large section so everyone can hear and see.

tips.title: Silly sounds
tips.text: Swap ‘splat’ for a squeak, a roar or a festive ‘ho ho ho’.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a slower pace and let players point rather than speak.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a second person in the middle, or require players to say the other person’s name as well as splat.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version and let players use a gesture instead of ducking.

themedTwists.title: Pumpkin Splat
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a pumpkin gesture and a spooky ‘boo’ instead of splat.

themedTwists.title: Snowball Splat
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a pretend snowball throw and a ‘whoosh’ sound.

author: Games library team

title: Fruit Salad
summary: A chair-swapping game that gets everyone moving and listening for their fruit.
equipment: One chair per player, minus one
setup: Arrange the chairs in a circle facing inwards.
Give each player a fruit name: apple, banana, orange or strawberry.
Choose one player to stand in the middle without a chair.
steps: The player in the middle calls out a fruit. Everyone with that fruit must swap chairs.
The caller tries to sit in a free chair while the others swap.
If the caller says ‘fruit salad’, everyone must swap chairs.
Whoever is left without a chair becomes the next caller.
Play several rounds and change the fruit names to keep it fresh.
winning: There is no winner: the player left without a chair becomes the caller. For a competition, count how many times each player avoids being the caller.
safety: Walk, do not run. Chairs must stay in the circle and nobody should dive for a chair. Use chairs without arms for easy movement.

tips.title: Fewer fruits
tips.text: Start with two fruit names so the game is easy to follow.

tips.title: Big actions
tips.text: Give each fruit a silly action to do as they swap.

tips.title: Mix the group
tips.text: Change the fruit names each round so players sit next to different people.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use two fruits and let the caller stand in the middle without trying to steal a chair for the first round.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add more fruits or call two fruits at once.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use cushions on the floor or a seated circle with one spare spot, and let players swap places without chairs.

themedTwists.title: Christmas Dinner
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with sprouts, carrots, potatoes and pudding. ‘Christmas dinner’ means everyone swaps.

themedTwists.title: Jungle Salad
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with animal names and animal noises as players swap.

author: Games library team

title: Four Corners
summary: A simple guessing game where players choose a corner and hope the caller does not pick it.
setup: Put a numbered cone in each corner of the hall.
Choose one caller to stand in the middle with their eyes closed.
Explain that players must move quietly to a corner before the caller finishes counting.
steps: The caller closes their eyes and counts slowly to ten.
Everyone else quietly chooses a corner and stands in it.
On ten, the caller calls out a corner number without looking.
Everyone in that corner is out and sits to the side. The rest choose a new corner.
The last player left becomes the next caller.
winning: The last player remaining wins and becomes the next caller.
safety: Walking only, and keep the corners clear of furniture. Make sure players do not crowd or push into a corner.

tips.title: Number signs
tips.text: Use large numbered signs so everyone can see which corner is which.

tips.title: Sneaky caller
tips.text: The caller can pause before saying a number to build suspense.

tips.title: No peeking
tips.text: Have a leader stand near the caller to make sure they keep their eyes closed.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Count to five and let players choose their corner before the count starts.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Call two corners at once, or ask players to move in a silly walk.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players sit in a corner of their choice, and offer a ‘safe corner’ card that can be used once.

themedTwists.title: Haunted Houses
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with four haunted house signs and a spooky sound for each corner.

themedTwists.title: Space Stations
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with four space station names and a countdown from ten.

author: Games library team

title: Wink Murder
summary: A quiet detective game of winks, dramatic exits and careful observation.
setup: Sit everyone in a circle where they can see each other.
Prepare one ‘detective’ card, one ‘murderer’ card and enough ‘villager’ cards for everyone else.
Explain that players who are winked at must sit down quietly, not fall over.
steps: Everyone closes their eyes and picks a card. The detective reveals themselves, then closes their eyes again.
The murderer then reveals themselves to the detective, and everyone opens their eyes.
The murderer winks at villagers one at a time. A winked-at villager counts to three and sits down.
The detective watches for the wink and has three guesses to identify the murderer.
If the detective guesses correctly, the villagers win. If not, the murderer wins.
winning: The villagers win if the detective finds the murderer within three guesses. The murderer wins if they eliminate enough villagers first.
safety: No dramatic falling: players sit down gently. Make sure everyone can see the murderer’s face and that no one is left out of the circle.

tips.title: Quiet winks
tips.text: Ask the murderer to wink clearly but not obviously, and to avoid winking at the same person twice.

tips.title: Detective hints
tips.text: Let the detective ask one yes/no question before each guess.

tips.title: Short rounds
tips.text: Play three short rounds with different murderers rather than one long round.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer players and let the detective have five guesses.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘doctor’ who can revive one villager, or let the murderer wink twice per round.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use a small torch or a hand signal instead of a wink, and offer a seated circle with no movement needed.

themedTwists.title: Ghost in the Circle
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the murderer is a ghost and winked-at villagers float down to the floor.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Spy
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a naughty-or-nice list and a jingle bell for each guess.

author: Games library team

title: Human Knot
summary: A team challenge where the group must untangle themselves without letting go of each other’s hands.
setup: Split into groups of six to eight.
Ask each group to stand in a circle.
Explain that they must not let go of hands unless a leader says so.
steps: Each player puts their right hand into the middle and takes the hand of someone across the circle.
Then each player takes a different person’s hand with their left hand.
The group must now untangle themselves into a circle without letting go.
If the group is completely stuck, a leader can allow one pair to let go, turn around and rejoin.
Celebrate when the group makes a circle, or when they have made the best shape they can.
winning: The group wins when they are standing in a circle with everyone’s hands still linked. There is no race unless you choose to make it one.
safety: No pulling, twisting or lifting. Stop immediately if anyone feels uncomfortable. Make sure players can step over linked hands safely and keep the floor clear.

tips.title: Small groups
tips.text: Six to eight is the sweet spot. Bigger groups get tangled and frustrated.

tips.title: One step at a time
tips.text: Ask the group to plan their next move before they start pulling.

tips.title: Talk it out
tips.text: Encourage quieter players to give directions so everyone has a role.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use groups of four or five, or allow one pair to let go every two minutes.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Ask the group to untangle without talking, or to finish in a specific shape.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version using a rope loop, and let players choose to be the coach who guides the group.

themedTwists.title: Spaghetti Monster
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a spaghetti-monster story and silly slurping noises when the group gets stuck.

themedTwists.title: Space Tangle
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with astronauts linked by a ‘gravity rope’ and a countdown to untangle.

author: Games library team

title: Helium Stick
summary: A deceptively simple teamwork challenge: lower a light stick to the ground without anyone losing contact.
equipment: One light pole or broom handle per group
setup: Split into groups of five to eight.
Ask each group to stand in two lines facing each other.
Give each group a light pole and ask them to hold it with both index fingers underneath.
steps: The group must lower the pole to the floor as a team.
Everyone must keep both index fingers touching the pole at all times.
If anyone loses contact, the group stops and starts again from waist height.
The group can talk and plan, but nobody may grip the pole.
Once the group reaches the floor, try it again with a shorter time limit.
winning: The group wins when the pole touches the floor with every player still touching it. For a challenge, time each attempt and try to beat it.
safety: Use a light pole and keep feet clear. Do not drop the pole on anyone’s toes, and do not let players push down on each other’s fingers.

tips.title: Finger contact
tips.text: Ask players to use the sides of their index fingers, not the tips, so the pole does not roll away.

tips.title: One voice
tips.text: Encourage one person to count or give instructions so the group moves together.

tips.title: Reset quickly
tips.text: Make restarts fast and light-hearted so the group does not get discouraged.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a longer pole, fewer players, or allow one person to guide without touching.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Ask the group to lower the pole without talking, or to do it while standing on one leg.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use a shorter pole for smaller hands, and let players support the pole with flat palms instead of fingers.

themedTwists.title: Magic Wand
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the pole is a wizard’s wand that must be lowered into a cauldron.

themedTwists.title: Laser Beam
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a ‘laser beam’ that must be lowered into the docking bay without breaking contact.

author: Games library team

title: All Aboard
summary: A shrinking-island team challenge that asks the group to fit into less and less space.
equipment: One tarpaulin, sheet or newspaper sheet per group
setup: Split into groups of four to six.
Give each group a tarp or a large sheet of newspaper.
Mark a clear space for each group on the floor.
steps: The whole group must stand on their island with nobody touching the floor.
Count to ten together while everyone stays on board.
Fold the island in half and try again.
Keep folding until the group can no longer fit.
The group that can fit on the smallest island wins.
winning: The group that keeps everyone on the smallest folded island wins.
safety: No jumping, stacking or carrying players. Keep the floor dry and clear, and let players step off carefully when the island gets too small.

tips.title: Team shapes
tips.text: Encourage the group to plan their shape before they step on the island.

tips.title: Hold hands
tips.text: Linking hands can help balance, but nobody should pull anyone off balance.

tips.title: Small steps
tips.text: Fold the island in smaller stages so groups have more chances to succeed.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Start with a bigger island and fold it more slowly.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Ask the group to stay silent, or to keep one player’s feet off the island entirely.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Allow players to sit on the edge with their feet on the island, and let anyone who prefers not to balance be the counter or coach.

themedTwists.title: Space Station Evacuation
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the island is a space station and each fold is a meteor strike.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Raft
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a sinking raft and a pirate countdown before each fold.

author: Games library team

title: River Crossing
summary: A classic team challenge: cross the crocodile-infested river using only a few floating mats.
equipment: 2–3 mats or large pieces of cardboard per group
setup: Mark a river area about five to eight metres wide.
Give each group two or three mats.
Scatter beanbags in the river as crocodiles.
steps: The group must get everyone from one bank to the other without touching the floor.
Players can only stand on the mats. Mats can be moved, but nobody may step into the river.
If a player touches the floor or a crocodile, the whole group returns to the start.
The group must work together to move the mats forward and bring everyone across.
For a bigger challenge, add a rule that one player must always be in contact with each mat.
winning: The first group to get every player across safely wins. If it is not a race, the group wins by completing the crossing together.
safety: Use non-slip mats and keep the floor dry. No dragging or carrying players, and no jumping between mats. Make sure there is space for groups to cross without colliding.

tips.title: Plan first
tips.text: Give each group one minute to plan before they start moving.

tips.title: Crocodile spots
tips.text: Place crocodiles so groups have to change their route, not just walk straight across.

tips.title: Talk it through
tips.text: After the game, ask each group what worked and what they would change next time.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter river, more mats, or allow one player to stand on the bank and guide.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Remove a mat, add a time limit, or require the whole group to stay silent.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players cross on a scooter board or with a buddy, and allow anyone who prefers not to balance to be the route planner.

themedTwists.title: Mars Crossing
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the river is a crater field and the mats are moon boots.

themedTwists.title: Swamp Crossing
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with crocodiles, vines and a jungle soundtrack.

author: Games library team

title: Toxic Waste
summary: A team challenge that needs steady hands and good communication to move a bucket of ‘toxic waste’.
setup: Fill a bucket with balls and place it inside a marked circle.
Mark a safe zone a few metres away.
Tie ropes to the bucket handle and lay them outside the circle.
steps: The group must move the bucket from the toxic zone to the safe zone without entering the circle.
Players stand outside the circle and use the ropes to lift and guide the bucket.
If any balls spill, the group must stop and put them back before carrying on.
Nobody may touch the bucket with their hands or step inside the toxic zone.
For an extra challenge, add a second bucket that must be moved at the same time.
winning: The group wins when the bucket and all its contents are safely inside the target zone.
safety: Do not wrap ropes around hands or wrists. Pull gently and keep fingers away from the bucket handle. Use a light bucket and soft balls, and keep the area clear.

tips.title: One voice
tips.text: Ask the group to choose a caller who counts the lifts and gives directions.

tips.title: Small movements
tips.text: Encourage tiny adjustments rather than big pulls.

tips.title: Spotters
tips.text: Have two players act as spotters who watch the bucket and warn the group.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter distance, more ropes, or a bucket with a wider handle.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add obstacles between the zones, or require the group to stay silent.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players hold a rope with a buddy, and allow anyone who prefers not to pull to be the caller or spotter.

themedTwists.title: Alien Slime
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but the bucket is a container of alien slime that must be returned to the mothership.

themedTwists.title: Witch’s Brew
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a cauldron, glowing balls and a spell to recite before each lift.

author: Games library team

title: Human Tic Tac Toe
summary: A relay race version of noughts and crosses that gets teams thinking and sprinting.
equipment: 6 beanbags or bibs (3 of each colour)
setup: Lay out nine hoops in a 3x3 grid.
Put a start line a few metres away.
Give each team three beanbags of the same colour.
steps: Teams line up behind the start line with their three beanbags.
One player from each team runs to the grid and places a beanbag in a hoop.
They run back and tag the next player, who places the next beanbag.
The first team to get three of their beanbags in a row wins the round.
If all six beanbags are placed and nobody has won, players take turns moving one of their own beanbags to a new hoop.
winning: The first team to make a row of three wins the round. Play the best of three rounds.
safety: Walk or jog, and make sure players run around the grid rather than through it. Keep the start line clear and use soft beanbags.

tips.title: Team huddles
tips.text: Let teams plan their first three moves before the race starts.

tips.title: Two grids
tips.text: Use two grids side by side so both teams can play at once without colliding.

tips.title: Change the grid
tips.text: Make the grid bigger for younger groups so there is more space to run.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a 2x2 grid, or let players place their beanbag without running back to tag.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘move one piece per turn’ rule from the start, or require players to hop between hoops.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players place their beanbag from the start line, and allow anyone who prefers not to run to be the team tactician.

themedTwists.title: Superhero Showdown
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with superhero names for each team and a power pose before every move.

themedTwists.title: Pumpkin Patch
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with orange and black beanbags and a spooky cackle for every winning row.

author: Games library team

title: Parachute Popcorn
summary: A joyful parachute game that turns soft balls into popping popcorn.
setup: Spread the parachute on the floor and ask everyone to hold an edge.
Put the soft balls in the middle.
Practise a gentle lift and shake together.
steps: Everyone lifts the parachute and shakes it gently to make the balls pop.
Try to keep all the popcorn on the parachute.
Count how many balls fall off in one minute.
Try a second round with a rule: no balls may touch the floor.
Finish with a calm round where everyone lowers the parachute slowly to the floor.
winning: There is no winner: the aim is to keep the popcorn popping. For a challenge, count how many balls stay on the parachute for a full minute.
safety: Keep the parachute low and do not let anyone go underneath without a signal. No pulling or running with the parachute, and use soft balls only.

tips.title: Small shakes
tips.text: Gentle, fast shakes work better than big lifts.

tips.title: Count together
tips.text: Count the popcorn aloud as a group to keep everyone involved.

tips.title: Calm finish
tips.text: End with a slow ‘popcorn settling’ round to bring the energy down.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer balls and a smaller parachute, or let players hold the edge with two hands.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a rule that players must swap places after every pop, or use lighter balls.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version with the parachute on laps, and let players choose to be the counter or ball collector.

themedTwists.title: Popping Pumpkins
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with orange balls and a witch’s cackle every time a pumpkin pops off.

themedTwists.title: Snowstorm
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with white balls and a gentle ‘brrr’ as the snow falls.

author: Games library team

title: Tug of War
summary: The ultimate team pull: two teams, one rope and a lot of noise.
equipment: Tape or ribbon for the centre mark
setup: Mark a centre line and a pulling line on each side.
Lay the rope along the centre line with the middle marker over the centre line.
Split into two even teams and line them up on opposite sides.
steps: Each team picks up the rope and stands behind their pulling line.
On the count of three, both teams pull backwards.
The team that pulls the centre marker past their own pulling line wins the round.
Best of three rounds wins the match.
Swap one or two players between teams between rounds to keep teams balanced.
winning: The team that pulls the centre marker past their line wins the round. The team that wins two rounds wins the match.
safety: Never wrap the rope around hands or wrists. Wear suitable footwear, keep fingers clear of the rope end, and stop immediately if anyone slips. Do not let go suddenly at the end of a round.

tips.title: Even teams
tips.text: Balance teams by size and strength, not just numbers.

tips.title: One rhythm
tips.text: Ask a leader to call ‘pull, pull, pull’ so the team pulls together.

tips.title: Short rounds
tips.text: Keep each pull short and give teams a rest between rounds.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter rope, fewer players, or a ‘sit-down pull’ for younger groups.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a rule that the whole team must stay silent, or pull with one hand.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated rope pull for players who prefer not to stand, and let others be the count caller or line judges.

themedTwists.title: Grinch’s Tug
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a ‘stolen Christmas’ story and a festive countdown.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Tug
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with pirate names for each team and a treasure chest marker.

author: Games library team

title: Balloon Volleyball
summary: A gentle, funny volleyball game that keeps everyone moving without a hard ball.
setup: Stretch a rope or net across the middle of the hall at about waist height.
Mark a court on each side with cones.
Split into two teams.
steps: One team serves the balloon over the rope.
Teams can use any part of their body to keep the balloon in the air, but cannot catch or hold it.
A team gets a point when the balloon lands on the other team’s floor.
Players can take up to three touches before sending the balloon back over.
First team to ten points wins, then swap sides.
winning: The first team to reach ten points wins. Play the best of three games.
safety: Use a balloon rather than a ball, and keep the floor clear. No diving or sliding, and do not stomp on fallen balloons. Check for latex allergies and have a foil balloon alternative.

tips.title: Keep it slow
tips.text: Balloon volleyball works best when teams work together rather than smashing it over.

tips.title: Count aloud
tips.text: Count the touches together so everyone knows when the ball must go over.

tips.title: Rotate
tips.text: Swap positions every few points so everyone gets a turn at the front.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a larger balloon, lower the rope, or allow players to catch and throw.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Allow only two touches, or require every player to touch the balloon before it goes over.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version with a lower net, and let players choose to be a scorer or line judge.

themedTwists.title: Ghost Balloons
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with white balloons decorated as ghosts and spooky music between points.

themedTwists.title: Space Balloon
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a countdown before each serve and slow-motion moon moves.

author: Games library team

title: Indoor Hockey
summary: A fast, safe version of hockey for the hall, using light sticks and a soft ball.
setup: Mark a pitch with cones and a goal at each end.
Split into two teams and give out bibs and sticks.
Demonstrate keeping the stick below waist height.
steps: Teams pass and dribble the ball with their sticks and try to score in the opposition goal.
Sticks must stay below waist height at all times.
No hitting, pushing or lifting the stick. Use a push pass rather than a swing.
A goal is scored when the ball crosses the goal line.
Rotate goalkeepers every few minutes and restart from the centre after each goal.
winning: The team with the most goals at the end of the match wins.
safety: Use soft balls and plastic sticks. Keep sticks below waist height, keep a stick’s length away from other players, and stop play if anyone is swinging their stick. Check sticks for cracks before the game.

tips.title: Small teams
tips.text: Four or five a side keeps the game open and reduces stick clashes.

tips.title: Push pass
tips.text: Practise push passes before the game so players do not swing at the ball.

tips.title: Rotate
tips.text: Swap positions every few minutes so everyone gets a turn on the ball.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a larger goal, a lighter ball, or play with no goalkeepers.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘three touches maximum’ rule, or require a pass before every goal.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a walking-only version and let players choose to be a goalkeeper, referee or scorer.

themedTwists.title: Wizards’ Hockey
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with broomsticks for sticks and a ‘flying’ celebration after each goal.

themedTwists.title: Reindeer Hockey
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with antlers and a red ball for Rudolph’s nose.

author: Games library team

title: Rounders
summary: A summer favourite: bat, run the bases and score rounders before the fielding team gets you out.
setup: Set out the four bases in a diamond and mark the boundary.
Split into two teams: batting and fielding.
Walk through the bases and the no-go area around the batter.
steps: The batter stands at the batting square and hits the ball when it is bowled.
After a hit, the batter runs around the bases and tries to reach the fourth post.
Fielders can get the batter out by catching a hit on the full, stumping the base they are running to, or hitting the base before the runner arrives.
A rounder is scored when a batter completes the full circuit and touches the fourth post.
After three outs, the teams swap roles.
winning: The team with the most rounders after an agreed number of innings wins.
safety: Use a soft ball and keep bats away from the waiting area. No throwing at runners, and keep spectators behind the boundary. Check the ground for holes and glass before playing.

tips.title: Small-sided
tips.text: Play with six to eight fielders so everyone gets more turns.

tips.title: Rotate positions
tips.text: Change fielding positions every innings so nobody is stuck in the deep field.

tips.title: Simplify
tips.text: For younger groups, remove the bowling and let batters hit from a tee.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a larger bat, a tee, and only three bases.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a rule that batters must run on every hit, or fielders must throw to first base before runners can move.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Use a soft ball and allow a buddy runner. Players who prefer not to bat can be umpires, scorers or fielding coaches.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Rounders
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with treasure chest bases and a ‘walk the plank’ celebration for every rounder.

themedTwists.title: Space Rounders
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planet bases and a countdown before each hit.

author: Games library team

title: Manhunt
summary: A thrilling wide game of hiding, seeking and jailbreaks for longer evenings and camps.
equipment: Hi-vis vests for seekers and marshals
setup: Set clear boundaries and walk them with the group.
Choose two or three seekers and give them hi-vis vests.
Place adult marshals at key points and agree a meeting point.
steps: The seekers count to 30 while everyone else hides within the boundary.
The seekers then search for the hiders and tag them.
Tagged hiders go to the jail area and wait to be rescued by a teammate.
A hider can free a teammate by reaching the jail and tagging them, but they must not be seen by a seeker.
The round ends when all hiders are caught or when time is called.
winning: The seekers win if they catch everyone. The hiders win if at least one player is still free when time is called.
safety: Keep boundaries away from roads, water and steep ground. No running in the dark without a torch, no hiding in unsafe places, and keep a headcount before, during and after. Use adult marshals and a whistle signal to end the game.

tips.title: Safe hiding spots
tips.text: Walk the boundary and point out areas that are out of bounds before the game starts.

tips.title: Shorter rounds
tips.text: Ten-minute rounds work better than one long game, especially for younger groups.

tips.title: Buddy system
tips.text: Ask everyone to play in pairs and stay with their buddy.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a smaller area, more seekers, or a shorter hiding time.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘no talking’ rule for hiders, or make the jail harder to reach.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players who prefer not to run be marshals, jail guards or radio callers. Offer a base game with a shorter boundary.

themedTwists.title: Ghost Hunt
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with ghostly hiders and torches covered with red film for a spooky glow.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Elves
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with elves hiding presents and seekers trying to find them before midnight.

author: Games library team

title: Sardines
summary: A reverse hide-and-seek game where everyone ends up squashed into the same hiding place.
setup: Choose one player to hide first.
Agree clear boundaries and a meeting point.
Send everyone else to a base to count to 30.
steps: One player hides while everyone else counts.
The seekers split up and search for the hidden player.
When a seeker finds the hider, they quietly join them in the hiding place.
Everyone keeps squeezing in until the last seeker finds the group.
The last person to find the group becomes the next hider.
winning: The last person to find the group wins and gets to hide next.
safety: Set boundaries and keep them away from roads, water and dark or unsafe areas. Make sure hiding places are safe and not too cramped. Tell a leader where the group is, and do a headcount at the end.

tips.title: Quiet entry
tips.text: Ask players to join the hiding place silently so the game lasts longer.

tips.title: Safe spaces
tips.text: Point out the best hiding spots before the game starts.

tips.title: Buddy up
tips.text: For younger groups, let players search in pairs.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a smaller area and give hints after five minutes.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a rule that hiders must move to a new hiding place every few minutes.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players who prefer not to hide be the timekeeper or the person who checks the group is safe.

themedTwists.title: Ghost Sardines
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with ghostly whispers and a torch under a sheet at the hiding place.

themedTwists.title: Elf Sardines
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a jingle bell at the hiding place and elf hats for the seekers.

author: Games library team

title: Pirate Treasure Hunt
summary: A clue-following adventure with a map, checkpoints and a treasure at the end.
setup: Hide clue cards around the outdoor area.
Draw a simple map with the checkpoints marked.
Split into small groups and give each group a bag and a map.
steps: Each group follows the map to the first checkpoint and solves the clue.
The clue sends them to the next checkpoint.
At each checkpoint, an adult marshal stamps or initials their card.
The final clue leads to the treasure.
Groups return to the meeting point and share what they found.
winning: Every group wins when they find the treasure. If you want a race, the first group back with all their stamps wins.
safety: Keep checkpoints within clear boundaries and away from roads and water. Put an adult at each checkpoint or keep the area small. Check food allergies before giving out any treats.

tips.title: Picture clues
tips.text: Use picture clues for Beavers and simple riddles for Cubs.

tips.title: Team roles
tips.text: Give each group a map reader, a clue collector and a timekeeper.

tips.title: Spare treasure
tips.text: Have enough treasure for every group so nobody goes home empty-handed.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a small area, picture clues and an adult with each group.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a puzzle to solve at each checkpoint, or make the map less detailed.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a shorter route and let players choose roles that suit them. Use allergy-friendly treasure.

themedTwists.title: Space Treasure
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planet checkpoints and ‘moon rock’ treasure.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Stocking Hunt
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with Christmas clues and a stocking at the end.

author: Games library team

title: Nature Scavenger Hunt
summary: A calm outdoor challenge that encourages close looking, teamwork and respect for nature.
setup: Choose an outdoor area with a mix of trees, grass and paths.
Give each group a list and a clipboard.
Explain the ‘look, don’t pick’ rule.
steps: Groups explore the area and tick off items from their list.
They can draw or photograph items they cannot collect.
Only fallen leaves, twigs and stones may be collected. Nothing living should be picked.
Groups meet back at the base and share their favourite find.
For a challenge, give points for teamwork and careful observation as well as finds.
winning: Every group wins by completing their list. If you want a competition, award points for the most items found and the best team drawing.
safety: Keep within boundaries and supervise closely. Do not taste anything, wash hands afterwards, and leave wildlife and flowers where they are. Check for allergies before handling natural materials.

tips.title: Different lists
tips.text: Give each group a slightly different list so they explore different areas.

tips.title: Draw it
tips.text: Encourage drawing as well as ticking so the hunt works even without collecting.

tips.title: Leave no trace
tips.text: Finish by checking the area and taking everything home.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a short list with pictures and a small area.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a time limit, or ask groups to find something for every letter of the alphabet.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a sensory list with textures and sounds, and let players choose to be the recorder or photographer.

themedTwists.title: World Safari
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with continents to match to the natural items you find.

themedTwists.title: Jungle Explorer
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with explorer names and a jungle sound hunt.

author: Games library team

title: Photo Orienteering
summary: A team navigation challenge where players use photos instead of maps to find checkpoints.
equipment: A camera or tablet per group
setup: Take close-up photos of six to eight landmarks around the site.
Place a numbered marker at each landmark.
Split into groups and give each group the photo set and a map.
steps: Groups use the photos to work out where each checkpoint is.
At each checkpoint, they write down the number on the marker.
Groups take a team photo at each checkpoint as proof.
The first group to find all the checkpoints and return wins.
Review the photos together at the end and share the best team shot.
winning: The first group to find every checkpoint and return with the correct numbers wins.
safety: Set clear boundaries, keep checkpoints away from roads and water, and put an adult at any tricky point. Make sure players carry a whistle and know the meeting point.

tips.title: Close-ups
tips.text: Use close-up photos so groups have to look carefully rather than just run to obvious places.

tips.title: Team roles
tips.text: Give each group a photographer, a map reader and a timekeeper.

tips.title: Check the route
tips.text: Walk the route yourself before the game to check it is safe and achievable.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer checkpoints, wider photos and a small area.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Use close-up photos with no map, or add a puzzle at each checkpoint.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a shorter route and let players choose to be the photographer or the note-taker.

themedTwists.title: Space Mission Photos
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planet names for checkpoints and a mission log to complete.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Map
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a treasure map and a gold coin at each checkpoint.

author: Games library team

title: Charades
summary: A classic guessing game that works with any theme and any size of group.
setup: Split into two or more teams.
Prepare a list of prompts suitable for the group.
Agree on the rules: no talking, no mouthing words, no pointing at objects in the room.
steps: One player from a team comes to the front and picks a prompt.
They act it out without speaking while their team guesses.
The team gets one point if they guess correctly within the time limit.
Teams take turns, and the team with the most points after five rounds wins.
Let players suggest prompts for the final round.
winning: The team with the most points after an agreed number of rounds wins.
safety: Keep the acting area clear and ask players not to climb on furniture. Make sure prompts are age-appropriate and that nobody is forced to perform.

tips.title: Act in pairs
tips.text: Let shy players act in pairs so they are not alone at the front.

tips.title: Category clues
tips.text: Write the category on the card so teams know where to start guessing.

tips.title: Silly prompts
tips.text: Use prompts the group will find funny, not just film titles.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow sound effects and use picture prompts.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Ban hand gestures, or give teams only 30 seconds.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a drawing version or a ‘describe it without saying the word’ version. Let players choose their role.

themedTwists.title: Jungle Charades
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with jungle animals, explorers and jungle sounds.

themedTwists.title: Space Charades
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planets, aliens and astronaut jobs.

themedTwists.title: Around the World Charades
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with countries, landmarks and travel actions.

author: Games library team

title: Simon Says
summary: The simple listening game that proves how hard it is to do two things at once.
setup: Stand everyone in a clear space where they can see the leader.
Practise three simple actions together.
Explain that players only copy a command if it starts with ‘Simon says’.
steps: The leader calls out an action, sometimes starting with ‘Simon says’ and sometimes not.
Players only do the action if they hear ‘Simon says’. Anyone who moves without it does a quick forfeit and rejoins.
Speed up the commands and mix in silly actions.
Let a confident player take a turn as Simon.
Finish with a slow round to calm the group down.
winning: There is no winner: players who make a mistake do a forfeit and rejoin. For a competition, the last player still following the rules correctly wins.
safety: Use simple movements and keep the space clear. Avoid actions that involve jumping into other people or touching the floor with heads.

tips.title: Demonstrate
tips.text: Do the action yourself so players can copy, but keep the ‘Simon says’ trick clear.

tips.title: Silly actions
tips.text: Use actions the group finds funny: roar like a lion, make a pizza, do a robot dance.

tips.title: Young leaders
tips.text: Let a Beaver be Simon for a round while an adult helps with the commands.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use only three actions and always say ‘Simon says’ for the first few rounds.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘do the opposite’ round, or give commands faster.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version with arm actions, and let players choose to be the caller.

themedTwists.title: Santa Says
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with festive actions like wrapping a present or loading a sleigh.

themedTwists.title: Astronaut Says
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with floating, moonwalking and alien greetings.

author: Games library team

title: Egg and Spoon Race
summary: A classic balancing relay that is much harder than it looks.
setup: Mark a start line and a turning cone for each team.
Give each team a spoon and an egg.
Split into teams of four to six.
steps: The first player balances the egg on the spoon and walks to the turning cone.
They walk around the cone and back to their team.
They pass the spoon and egg to the next player without using their hands.
If the egg falls, the player picks it up, puts it back on the spoon and carries on from where they stopped.
The first team to finish every player wins.
winning: The first team to complete the relay with every player wins.
safety: Use plastic or hard-boiled eggs, not raw eggs. Walk, do not run, and keep the relay lanes clear. Check for egg allergies and wash hands after handling.

tips.title: Big spoons
tips.text: Use larger spoons for younger groups to make balancing easier.

tips.title: Two lanes
tips.text: Set up separate lanes so teams do not collide.

tips.title: Silly walk
tips.text: Add a silly walk for the return leg to keep it light-hearted.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a bigger spoon and a shorter course, or let players hold the egg with one finger.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add obstacles, or require players to balance the egg on the back of their hand.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a two-person carry option and let players choose to be the timekeeper or cone marshal.

themedTwists.title: Pumpkin and Spoon
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with small orange balls as pumpkins.

themedTwists.title: Bauble and Spoon
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with unbreakable baubles and a Christmas song at the finish line.

author: Games library team

title: Santa Relay
summary: A festive team relay where players race to turn a teammate into Santa.
setup: Put a pile of Santa kit at the far end of the hall for each team.
Mark a start line and a turning point.
Split into teams of four to six.
steps: One player from each team is the Santa and stands at the far end of the hall.
The first runner takes one item from the kit, runs to their Santa and helps them put it on, then runs back.
The next runner takes another item and adds it to the same Santa.
Continue until each team’s Santa is fully dressed.
The finished Santa must shout ‘ho ho ho’ to complete the round. The first team to finish wins.
winning: The first team to dress their Santa and complete a ‘ho ho ho’ wins.
safety: Do not cover faces or restrict breathing. Use loose clothing and help younger players dress. Keep the running lanes clear and avoid long costumes that could trip players.

tips.title: Team Santa
tips.text: Let the team choose one player to be Santa before the race starts.

tips.title: Easy kit
tips.text: Use items that are quick to put on: a hat, a bib, a scarf and a cushion.

tips.title: Photo finish
tips.text: Take a team photo of each finished Santa.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer items and a shorter course.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a wrapped present that must be carried without dropping.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let players choose to be the Santa, the dresser or the runner, and offer a seated dressing version.

themedTwists.title: Snowman Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with scarves, hats and paper snowballs to build a snowman.

themedTwists.title: Elf Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with pointy hats and a present to deliver at the finish.

author: Games library team

title: Pumpkin Relay
summary: A Halloween relay that turns a simple carry-and-weave race into a pumpkin challenge.
equipment: Small orange balls or soft pumpkins
setup: Set up a slalom of cones for each team.
Put a bucket at the end of each slalom.
Give each team a pumpkin and a spoon.
steps: The first player balances the pumpkin on the spoon and weaves through the cones.
They drop the pumpkin into the bucket at the end and run back.
The next player runs to the bucket, collects the pumpkin and weaves back.
The relay continues until every player has had a turn.
The first team to finish wins.
winning: The first team to complete the relay with every player wins.
safety: Walk rather than run, and use soft pumpkins or balls. Keep the slalom lanes wide enough for players to pass, and make sure the buckets are stable.

tips.title: Wide gates
tips.text: Set the cones wide apart for younger groups.

tips.title: Two hands
tips.text: Let Beavers use two hands on the spoon for extra balance.

tips.title: Spooky music
tips.text: Play Halloween music and restart the music every time a pumpkin drops.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter slalom and a bigger spoon, or carry the pumpkin in a bucket.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a second pumpkin, or require players to carry the spoon on the back of their hand.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a two-person carry option and let players choose to be the timekeeper or cone marshal.

themedTwists.title: Witch’s Hat Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, but players wear a witch’s hat while they weave.

themedTwists.title: Watermelon Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a green ball as a watermelon and a summer picnic at the finish.

author: Games library team

title: Easter Egg Hunt
summary: A classic hunt with clues, teams and a count-at-the-end twist.
setup: Hide the eggs around a clear outdoor area.
Set boundaries and walk them with the group.
Split into small groups and give each group a bag and a clue card.
steps: Groups follow the clues to find the eggs.
Each group collects only the eggs in their colour or with their group’s sticker.
When the time is up, groups return to the meeting point and count their eggs.
Award prizes for the most eggs, the best teamwork and the best clue-solving.
Check that every group found at least one egg.
winning: There is no single winner: every group wins by finding their eggs. For a competition, the group with the most eggs wins.
safety: Keep the hunt within clear boundaries and away from roads and water. Check food allergies before giving out treats, and make sure younger groups are accompanied by an adult.

tips.title: Colour-coded
tips.text: Give each group a colour so they only collect their own eggs.

tips.title: Picture clues
tips.text: Use picture clues for Beavers and riddles for Cubs.

tips.title: Spare eggs
tips.text: Hide a few extra eggs so every group can find something.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a small area, large eggs and picture clues.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a puzzle to solve before each clue, or hide the eggs in trickier places.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a shorter route and allergy-friendly prizes. Let players choose to be the clue reader or the counter.

themedTwists.title: Space Egg Hunt
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planet-shaped eggs and a countdown to blast-off.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Egg Hunt
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a treasure map and golden eggs.

author: Games library team

title: Jungle Animal Relay
summary: A noisy, silly relay where teams move like different jungle animals.
setup: Mark a start line and a turning cone for each team.
Prepare animal cards with a different animal for each leg.
Split into teams of four to six.
steps: The first player picks an animal card and moves to the cone and back like that animal.
They tag the next player, who picks a new animal card.
Continue until every player has had a turn.
For the final leg, the whole team moves together like the same animal.
The first team to finish wins.
winning: The first team to complete every animal leg wins.
safety: Demonstrate each animal move and keep the lanes clear. Avoid moves that involve crawling into other players or jumping onto furniture. Walking versions work just as well.

tips.title: Silly sounds
tips.text: Ask players to make the animal noise as they move.

tips.title: Choose together
tips.text: Let each team choose their final animal.

tips.title: Wide lanes
tips.text: Set the cones wide apart so animals do not crash into each other.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use simple moves like stomping, flapping or hopping.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘move backwards’ animal or a ‘carry an egg’ animal.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer seated animal actions and let players choose to be the animal caller or judge.

themedTwists.title: Safari Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with animals from different continents.

themedTwists.title: Polar Animal Relay
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with penguins, polar bears and seals.

author: Games library team

title: Superhero Training
summary: An obstacle-course challenge where recruits earn their superhero stripes.
setup: Set up a circuit of four or five stations: jumping, balancing, throwing and crawling.
Put mats under any jumping or crawling stations.
Split into small groups and give each group a scorecard.
steps: Each group visits every station and completes the challenge.
A leader marks their scorecard when the whole group completes the station.
Stations can include: hoop hop, beanbag target throw, balance beam, tunnel crawl and a superhero pose.
Groups rotate every three minutes.
The group with the most completed stations wins, or everyone earns a superhero certificate.
winning: Every group wins by completing the circuit. For a competition, the group with the most station points wins.
safety: Use mats for jumps and crawls, and check the equipment before starting. No jumping from height, and keep the stations spaced out so groups do not collide.

tips.title: Demonstrate
tips.text: Show each station before the groups start, and let a young leader demonstrate.

tips.title: Teamwork points
tips.text: Award extra points for helping each other and cheering.

tips.title: Certificates
tips.text: Finish with a superhero certificate for every recruit.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer stations, lower jumps and bigger targets.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a time limit per station or a ‘no talking’ challenge.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer seated station options and let players choose to be the timekeeper, scorekeeper or station coach.

themedTwists.title: Space Cadet Training
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with astronaut training stations and a mission patch for each recruit.

themedTwists.title: Pirate Training
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with ship-board challenges and a pirate oath at the end.

author: Games library team

title: Around the World Relay
summary: A relay that takes teams across the continents without leaving the hall.
setup: Set up a station for each continent around the hall.
Put a different movement challenge at each station.
Give each team a passport sheet.
steps: Teams start at the first continent and complete the movement challenge.
A leader stamps their passport and they move to the next continent.
Challenges can include hopping across Australia, balancing through Africa and crawling through Asia.
The first team to collect all the stamps and return to the start wins.
Finish by sharing one fact about each continent.
winning: The first team to complete their passport and return to the start wins.
safety: Keep the stations spaced out and demonstrate each movement. Use mats for crawling and keep the floor clear.

tips.title: Passport stamps
tips.text: Use simple stickers or drawings for the passport stamps.

tips.title: Music
tips.text: Play music from around the world between stations.

tips.title: Facts
tips.text: Put a fun fact at each station so players learn something too.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use three continents and simple movements.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a puzzle at each continent before the team can move on.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer seated challenges and let players choose to be the passport stamper or station coach.

themedTwists.title: Space Race
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with planets instead of continents.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Journey
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with countries Santa visits on Christmas Eve.

author: Games library team

title: Human Foosball
summary: A team game that turns the classic table football formation into a full-body challenge.
setup: Mark a pitch with goals at each end.
Arrange each team in three rows of two or three players.
Explain that players must hold hands within their row and can only move side to side.
steps: Teams stand in rows facing the opposition goal and hold hands with their row.
Players can only move sideways along their row. They cannot move forward or backward.
The ball is kicked along the floor. No hands allowed, except the goalkeeper.
A goal is scored when the ball crosses the opposition goal line.
After a goal, both teams reset to their starting rows.
winning: The team with the most goals at the end of the match wins.
safety: Use a soft ball and keep the rows spaced out. No pulling hands or dragging teammates, and no sliding tackles. Keep the goals stable.

tips.title: Row roles
tips.text: Give each row a name so teams can plan who moves where.

tips.title: Rotate
tips.text: Swap rows every few minutes so everyone gets a turn at the front.

tips.title: Small teams
tips.text: Three rows of two is easier to manage than three rows of four.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a larger ball, wider goals and fewer rows.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Allow only one-touch passes, or require every row to touch the ball before a goal.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a walking-only version and let players choose to be a goalkeeper, referee or row coach.

themedTwists.title: Wizard Foosball
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with broomstick moves and a spell before every goal.

themedTwists.title: Reindeer Foosball
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with antlers and a sleigh-bell ball.

author: Games library team

title: Silent Line Up
summary: A communication challenge where the group must line up in order without speaking.
setup: Clear a space where the whole group can stand in a line.
Explain that the challenge must be completed without speaking.
Agree on a signal for ‘I need help’.
steps: The group must line up in order of birthday, height or shoe size without talking.
Players can use gestures, eye contact or written notes.
Once they think they are in order, they raise their hands.
Check the order together and celebrate the result.
Try a harder version with eyes closed or with a time limit.
winning: The group wins when everyone is in the correct order and nobody has spoken.
