safety: If using blindfolds, make sure players are supervised and have a buddy. Keep the floor clear and allow players to opt out of blindfolded versions.

tips.title: Start easy
tips.text: Begin with height, which is easy to see, before trying birthday order.

tips.title: Non-verbal signals
tips.text: Agree on a few gestures before starting, such as pointing to a month.

tips.title: Debrief
tips.text: Ask the group what was hard about communicating without words.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow whispering, or use a small group of six to eight.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a time limit, or ask the group to line up by birthday including the year.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer written notes or a picture board, and let players choose to be the organiser or the checker.

themedTwists.title: Elf Line Up
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with elf names and a Christmas list to organise.

themedTwists.title: Space Crew
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with astronauts lining up by mission number.

author: Games library team

title: Electric Fence
summary: A team challenge that asks the group to get everyone over an imaginary electric fence.
setup: Set up a rope between two poles at about waist height.
Put mats on both sides of the fence.
Mark a safe zone on each side.
steps: The group must get every player from one side of the fence to the other without touching the rope.
Players can help each other over, but nobody may go under the fence.
If anyone touches the rope, the whole group starts again.
Use mats and spotters for safety.
For a harder version, add a ‘no talking’ rule or a time limit.
winning: The group wins when everyone is safely on the other side without touching the fence.
safety: Use a soft rope and mats on both sides. No diving or dropping players, and always use spotters. Do not let players climb on each other’s shoulders, and check the ground for hazards.

tips.title: Plan first
tips.text: Give the group a minute to plan who will go first and who will spot.

tips.title: Spotters
tips.text: Assign two spotters who are not lifting anyone.

tips.title: Talk it through
tips.text: Ask the group what they would do differently next time.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Lower the rope, use a wider gap, or allow one player to cross at a time with help.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a time limit, or make the whole group cross without talking.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a ground-level version where players step over a line, and let anyone who prefers not to be lifted be a spotter or planner.

themedTwists.title: Laser Grid
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a laser grid to cross and a countdown to safety.

themedTwists.title: Dragon’s Lair
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a sleeping dragon and a treasure to reach.

author: Games library team

title: Marshmallow Tower
summary: A calm team challenge to build the tallest freestanding tower from spaghetti and marshmallows.
setup: Give each group a plate with 20 marshmallows, 20 spaghetti strands, 30cm of tape and 30cm of string.
Clear a flat area for each group.
Explain that the tower must stand on its own for 10 seconds.
steps: Groups have 15 minutes to build the tallest freestanding tower they can.
They can break the spaghetti but cannot use extra materials.
At the end of the time, each group measures their tower.
The tower must stand for 10 seconds without support.
Measure from the table to the highest point of the tower.
winning: The group with the tallest freestanding tower wins.
safety: Check for food allergies before using marshmallows. Do not eat the building materials, and be careful with broken spaghetti ends. Supervise younger groups closely.

tips.title: Plan first
tips.text: Give groups two minutes to plan before they start building.

tips.title: Strong base
tips.text: Encourage groups to build a wide base before adding height.

tips.title: Test early
tips.text: Ask groups to test their tower halfway through the time.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer materials and a shorter time, or allow a cardboard base.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Remove the tape and string, or require the tower to hold a small object on top.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Let groups assign roles: designer, builder, measurer and presenter. Offer a no-food alternative using straws and clay.

themedTwists.title: Space Tower
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a mission to build a tower on Mars and a countdown to launch.

themedTwists.title: Gingerbread Tower
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a festive story and a star on top of the winning tower.

author: Games library team

title: Paper Aeroplane Championship
summary: A design-and-fly challenge that turns a sheet of paper into a competition.
setup: Give everyone a sheet of paper and a marker.
Mark a throwing line and a runway.
Explain the two events: distance and accuracy.
steps: Everyone folds a paper aeroplane and decorates it.
For the distance event, players throw from the line and measure how far their plane lands.
For the accuracy event, players try to land their plane inside a hula hoop or target.
Each player gets three throws per event and keeps their best score.
Award prizes for distance, accuracy and best design.
winning: The player with the longest flight wins the distance event. The player closest to the target wins the accuracy event.
safety: Throw away from other players and keep the runway clear. No throwing at people, and use paper only, not card or sharp materials.

tips.title: Test and improve
tips.text: Give players time to test and adjust their design between throws.

tips.title: Two events
tips.text: Distance and accuracy give different designs a chance to win.

tips.title: Design prize
tips.text: Award a prize for the most creative plane, not just the best flyer.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Provide a simple pre-folded design and a short throwing distance.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘must fly through a hoop’ challenge, or limit the number of folds.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated throwing line and let players choose to be the designer, thrower or measurer.

themedTwists.title: Rocket Launch
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with rocket designs and a countdown before each throw.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Sleigh
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with sleigh designs and a ‘deliver the present’ target.

author: Games library team

title: Cup Stack Relay
summary: A speedy relay where teams race to build and knock down a pyramid of cups.
setup: Put a stack of cups on a table at the far end of the hall for each team.
Mark a start line and a turning point.
Split into teams of four to six.
steps: The first player runs to the table and builds a pyramid with the cups.
They run back and tag the next player.
The next player runs to the table and knocks the pyramid down.
The relay continues: build, knock down, build, knock down.
The first team to finish wins.
winning: The first team to complete the relay wins.
safety: Use plastic cups only and keep the table stable. Walk rather than run near the table, and keep the floor clear of fallen cups.

tips.title: Team order
tips.text: Let teams decide who builds and who knocks down.

tips.title: Big pyramid
tips.text: Use six cups for a simple pyramid or ten for a bigger challenge.

tips.title: Silly rules
tips.text: Add a ‘no hands’ round for extra laughs.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer cups and a shorter distance.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Require players to build with one hand, or add a ‘stack and balance a ball on top’ challenge.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated table version and let players choose to be the builder, knocker or timekeeper.

themedTwists.title: Pumpkin Stack
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with orange cups and a pumpkin on top of the winning pyramid.

themedTwists.title: Snowman Stack
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with white cups and a snowman face on the top cup.

author: Games library team

title: Sleeping Lions
summary: A calm-down game where the last lion to move wins.
setup: Ask everyone to lie down on the floor like sleeping lions.
Explain that lions must stay still and quiet.
Choose one or two leaders to be the ‘zookeepers’.
steps: The lions lie still with their eyes closed.
The zookeepers walk around trying to make them move or laugh without touching them.
A lion who moves becomes a zookeeper.
The last lion still lying still wins.
Finish with a slow stretch and a calm return to the circle.
winning: The last lion still lying still wins.
safety: No tickling or touching. Make sure the floor is clean and warm, and let players sit or use a mat if lying down is uncomfortable.

tips.title: Calm music
tips.text: Play quiet music to help everyone settle.

tips.title: Silly faces
tips.text: Zookeepers can pull funny faces, but no touching.

tips.title: Short rounds
tips.text: Two or three minutes is long enough for Beavers.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow small movements and keep rounds short.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Ask lions to keep a straight face while zookeepers tell jokes.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version and let players choose to be a zookeeper or a judge.

themedTwists.title: Sleeping Reindeer
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with reindeer antlers and a quiet Christmas story.

themedTwists.title: Sleeping Bats
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with bats hanging upside down (or sitting still) until sunrise.

author: Games library team

title: Snowball Siege
summary: A winter variant of French v English where teams throw beanbag snowballs and count up at the end.
setup: Lay the rope across the middle of the hall.
Split the snowballs equally between the two teams.
Put a bucket at the back of each team’s area.
steps: Teams start in their own half and may not cross the rope.
On ‘go’, players throw snowballs into the other team’s half.
Players can throw or roll the snowballs, but cannot carry them across the rope.
After two minutes, call ‘freeze!’ and count the snowballs in each half.
The team with the fewest snowballs in their half wins the round.
winning: The team with the fewest snowballs in their own half when time is called wins. Play three rounds and add up the scores.
safety: Use soft beanbags or paper snowballs only. No throwing at heads, and keep the area behind the buckets clear. Stop the game before players get too hot or tired.

tips.title: Count together
tips.text: Count the snowballs aloud with both teams so the result is clear.

tips.title: Clear buckets
tips.text: Use buckets at the back so snowballs do not roll under chairs.

tips.title: Quick rounds
tips.text: Two-minute rounds keep the energy high and the counting quick.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a shorter hall, fewer snowballs and a one-minute round.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a rule that players must throw with their non-dominant hand, or use one bucket as a target.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a rolling-only version and let players choose to be the counter or the snowball collector.

themedTwists.title: New Year Countdown
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a countdown from ten and a ‘midnight’ celebration at the end of each round.

author: Games library team

title: Zombie Dodgeball
summary: A Halloween variant of dodgeball where hit players rise again as zombies.
setup: Mark a centre line and two back lines.
Place the balls along the centre line.
Split into two teams.
steps: Play dodgeball as normal, but a player who is hit does not sit out.
Instead, they become a zombie and walk slowly around their own half with their arms out.
Zombies can tag active players who come within arm’s reach. A tagged player also becomes a zombie.
The last human standing wins for their team, or the team with the most humans when time is called.
Reset after each round and swap the starting zombie.
winning: The team with the most humans left when time is called wins. If one team has no humans left, the other team wins.
safety: Use soft foam balls and no headshots. Zombies must walk, not run, and tag gently. Keep the floor clear and make sure zombies do not corner players.

tips.title: Slow zombies
tips.text: Zombies must keep one arm out and walk slowly. It gives humans a chance.

tips.title: Clear zones
tips.text: Mark a ‘safe zone’ where humans can catch their breath for five seconds.

tips.title: Sound effects
tips.text: Encourage zombie groans and spooky music to set the scene.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use fewer balls, slower zombies and a larger safe zone.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘zombie respawn’ rule where zombies can return to their human form if they catch a ball.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a rolling-only version and let players choose to be a zombie from the start.

themedTwists.title: Mummy Dodgeball
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with toilet-paper mummies and a slower zombie walk.

title: Present Dash
summary: A Christmas variant of Capture the Flag where teams race to fill their sack with presents.
setup: Mark a central present pile and a sack for each team at opposite ends.
Set clear boundaries.
Split into two teams and place an adult marshal at each sack.
steps: On ‘go’, teams run to the central pile and take one present at a time back to their sack.
Players can only carry one present at a time.
Players can tag opponents in their own half. Tagged players go to the other team’s jail and can be freed by a teammate.
The first team to collect five presents in their sack wins.
If time runs out, the team with the most presents wins.
winning: The first team to collect five presents, or the team with the most presents when time is called, wins.
safety: Use soft presents and no tackling. Keep the central pile clear of feet, and walk the boundaries before starting. Put an adult at each jail.

tips.title: One at a time
tips.text: The one-present rule keeps the game fair and stops players hoarding.

tips.title: Team roles
tips.text: Ask teams to choose runners, defenders and rescuers.

tips.title: Count aloud
tips.text: Count the presents in each sack at the end so everyone can see the result.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Use a smaller area, fewer presents and no jail.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Add a ‘no running with a present’ rule, or hide presents around the area.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a walking-only version and let players choose to be a runner, guard or jail marshal.

themedTwists.title: Santa’s Sack
themedTwists.text: Same rules, with a Santa hat for the sack guard and a jingle bell on each present.

title: Crab Handball
summary: A crab-football variant that swaps kicking for throwing and catching.
setup: Mark a pitch with a goal at each end.
Split into two teams and give out bibs.
Demonstrate the crab position and a two-handed catch.
steps: Everyone plays in the crab position, moving on hands and feet with their chest facing the sky.
Players can throw, catch and roll the ball, but cannot stand up.
A goal is scored by throwing the ball between the opposition cones.
Players cannot snatch the ball from each other. Defenders must stay an arm’s length away.
Restart from the centre after each goal.
winning: The team with the most goals at the end of the match wins.
safety: Warm up wrists and shoulders. Use a soft ball and keep the floor clear. No tackling or grabbing, and take breaks if arms get tired.

tips.title: Short matches
tips.text: Play three-minute thirds with rests in between.

tips.title: Catch first
tips.text: Encourage a catch before every shot to slow the game down.

tips.title: Rotate
tips.text: Swap goalkeepers every few minutes.

adaptations.title: Make it easier
adaptations.text: Allow players to sit rather than hold the crab position, and use a larger goal.

adaptations.title: Make it harder
adaptations.text: Require three passes before a shot, or use a smaller ball.

adaptations.title: Include everyone
adaptations.text: Offer a seated version and let players choose to be a goalkeeper, referee or scorer.

themedTwists.text: Same rules, with spider names and a web-shaped goal.

themedTwists.text: Same rules, with slow-motion moon moves and a countdown before each restart.
